config.description: Engine start-up options. Changing these after the game has started has no effect until it is restarted.

game.description: Which game: 'doom' (the 1993 shareware episode, Knee-Deep in the Dead), 'heretic' (Raven's 1994 shareware episode, City of the Damned), 'hexen' (Beyond Heretic) or 'strife' (Quest for the Sigil). The module ships the Hexen and Strife engines but no IWAD for them: the operator's hexen.wad, or strife1.wad plus voices.wad, must be in the gateway's wads folder. All engines come from the same Chocolate Doom source; config.iwad / config.pwads then name that game's WADs.

autoStart.description: Start the engine as soon as the component mounts. Off shows a 'click to play' splash; the click also unlocks audio, which browsers only allow after a user gesture.

music.description: Music (OPL emulation). Off by default: it is CPU-hungry and E1M1 on loop tests the patience of coworkers.

iwad.description: Which IWAD to play. Empty = the bundled shareware one for config.game (doom1.wad or heretic1.wad). Otherwise the name of an IWAD the gateway operator placed in data/modules/com.mustrysolutions.doom/wads/ (e.g. 'doom2' for DOOM2.WAD, 'heretic' for HERETIC.WAD; case-insensitive, '.wad' optional). Unknown = shareware plus output.wadError. The module never ships registered WADs.

playerClass.description: Hexen only: the character class (-class). Ignored by Doom and Heretic.

pwads.description: PWADs (mods, map packs) from the same gateway folder, loaded in order after the IWAD (Chocolate Doom -file). A missing one is skipped and named in output.wadError.

skill.description: 1 = I'm too young to die ... 5 = Nightmare!

warp.description: Skip the title screen and start straight in the map given by config.episode / config.map.

episode.description: Episode to warp to. The shareware IWAD only has episode 1 (Knee-Deep in the Dead); Ultimate Doom has 4. Ignored for Doom II-style IWADs (MAP01..MAP32), which have no episodes.

map.description: Map to warp to: 1-9 within the episode for Doom-style IWADs, 1-32 for Doom II-style ones.

keyboard.description: Let the physical keyboard drive the game while the canvas has focus (click it first). Keys never reach the game while another element is focused, so the rest of the view keeps working. Off = tag-bound controls only.

mouse.description: Mouse look/turn while the canvas has focus.

pixelated.description: Scale the 320x200 frame with crisp nearest-neighbour pixels instead of smoothing. It is 1993, after all.

showHud.description: Show the component's own status strip under the canvas (engine state, last message, focus hint).

playLabel.description: Text on the splash button. Empty = 'Click to play'.

extraArgs.description: Extra command-line arguments passed to the engine, space-separated (e.g. '-nomonsters', '-fast', '-respawn'). Advanced.

statsIntervalMs.description: How often (ms) the live telemetry outputs are refreshed while the game runs.

persistSaves.description: Keep Doom's six save-game slots on the gateway per Perspective user (data/modules/com.mustrysolutions.doom/saves/<user>/). Slots are restored into the engine before it starts, so Doom's own Load Game menu shows them. Unauthenticated sessions keep saves in the tab only (no shared anonymous folder). Off = never persist.

player.description: Who this marine is, for the module's own [Doom] tag provider: telemetry lands in [Doom]Players/<player>/*. Empty = the session's authenticated user name, or anonymous-<session> when there is none.

publishTelemetry.description: Send the live telemetry to the gateway, which writes it into the module's [Doom] tag provider (Players/<player>/Health, Armor, Ammo, ...). No bindings needed.

multiplayer.description: Deathmatch over the gateway's relay (/system/doom-relay/<arena>). 'host' starts a server that launches the game once config.players marines have joined; 'join' connects to the arena's host. Everyone in an arena must use the same settings. The gateway issues each session a single-use admission ticket; only Perspective sessions running this component can reach an arena. Off = single player.

arena.description: Which relay arena to host or join. One host per arena; players in different arenas never meet.

players.description: Host only: how many marines (host included) before the game launches on its own.

deathmatch.description: Netgame rules: cooperative, deathmatch (weapons stay), or altdeath (weapons respawn, no suicide penalty). Heretic has no altdeath; it plays deathmatch.

relayUrl.description: Override the relay WebSocket URL. Empty derives ws(s)://<this gateway>/system/doom-relay/<arena> from the page's own address.

data.description: Tag-bindable controls. A true holds that key down for as long as it stays true, so a PLC input can drive the marine. 'weapon' selects a weapon slot on change (0 = none).

weapon.description: Weapon slot to select when this value changes (1-7). 0 = no change.

paused.description: Pause the engine's main loop. Bind it to an alarm: production stops, Doom stops.

running.description: Two-way. True starts the engine (same as clicking the splash), false quits it (Chocolate Doom's I_Quit). The component writes it back as the engine starts and stops, so a binding can restart the game without a page reload.

output.description: Read-only engine status and live player telemetry (polled a few times per second while running). Bind these to memory tags to historize the marine.

state.description: idle | loading | running | paused | exited | error | busy. 'busy' means another Doom instance already owns this session (one per browser page).

message.description: The last line the engine printed.

inLevel.description: True while a map is being played (not on the title, intermission or finale).

ammo.description: Ammo for the ready weapon; -1 for fist/chainsaw.

weapon.description: Ready weapon slot: 0 fist, 1 pistol, 2 shotgun, 3 chaingun, 4 rocket launcher, 5 plasma, 6 BFG, 7 chainsaw.

items.description: Items picked up on this map.

dead.description: True while the marine is dead.

savedSlots.description: How many save-game slots the gateway holds for this user (0-6).

saveOwner.description: The user whose save games are stored on the gateway; empty for an unauthenticated session (saves then stay in the tab).

lastSaveSlot.description: Slot (1-6) of the most recent save in this session; 0 = none yet.

lastSaveDescription.description: Name the player typed for the most recent save in this session.

iwad.description: The IWAD the running engine was started with ('doom1' for the bundled shareware episode).

wadError.description: Why config.iwad / config.pwads could not be honoured in full (file not on the gateway, no gateway channel). Empty when everything loaded. The game still starts: an unknown IWAD falls back to shareware, a missing PWAD is skipped.

availableWads.description: The WAD files the gateway has in data/modules/com.mustrysolutions.doom/wads/, as reported when the engine last started with a custom IWAD or PWAD.

player.description: The player name the gateway resolved for this session (the [Doom]Players/<player> folder).

inLobby.description: True while the netgame lobby waits for players (host: until config.players have joined).

playerClass.description: Hexen: the class in play, 0 fighter, 1 cleric, 2 mage (3 while porked). 0 for the other games.

gold.description: Strife: gold carried. 0 for the other games.

questFlags.description: Strife: the quest bit flags (which quests are done). 0 for the other games.

netPlayers.description: Marines in the netgame (0 in single player).
